projects.name: PremierPro Wedding Engine
projects.headline: From raw footage to a review-ready edit.
projects.summary: An integrated video-analysis and editing pipeline that turns multi-camera wedding footage into review-ready Adobe Premiere timelines.
projects.problem: Large multi-camera wedding projects require footage review, quality checks, content classification, synchronization, and sequencing before an editor can work with a useful timeline.
projects.role: I built and integrated CV/video-analysis subsystems, media utilities, and Premiere automation, and performance-tuned long-form processing within a long-running client engagement.
delivered: Footage quality analysis, obstruction checks, and clip-selection logic integrated into the editing workflow.
Scene/event categorization and deterministic sequencing rules feeding automated Premiere timeline generation.
Media normalization, synchronization utilities, and structured JSON/CSV outputs connecting the pipeline stages.
approach: Use model predictions to supply quality and content signals; use explicit rules to organize the edit.
Combine detector proposals, geometric filters, ConvNeXt verification, and temporal persistence for obstruction detection.
Profile processing stages before optimizing: GPU optical flow and batched inference addressed separate measured bottlenecks.
projects.result: A working client pipeline producing review-ready Premiere projects, with measured improvements in specific video-processing stages.
projects.metricNote: CUDA/OpenCV optical-flow acceleration reduced the measured workflow from roughly four hours to ninety minutes. This is not a benchmark of every stage or every input.
projects.secondaryNote: A separate orientation-detector optimization using GPU batch inference; not an end-to-end runtime reduction.
projects.growth: This work strengthened my ability to connect models, media formats, business rules, and application automation into one usable client workflow.

projects.name: Image-to-KG / Text-to-KG
projects.headline: Media becomes connected, searchable knowledge.
projects.summary: Local-first document and media ingestion with preserved provenance, Neo4j graph integration, and retrieve-then-rerank search.
projects.problem: Documents, images, video, and audio contain related information, but extraction and search become fragile when their source relationships, identities, and metadata are lost.
projects.role: I implemented multimodal ingestion and semantic-extraction stages, integrated media and text graph layers, worked on retrieval/reranking, and ported the Windows pipeline to Apple Silicon.
delivered: PDF/media extraction, OCR handling, deduplication, and provenance manifests linking outputs back to source material.
Image, video, audio, and metadata processing feeding a Neo4j-backed knowledge graph.
Media/text entity integration and a retrieval workflow combining candidate signals with semantic reranking.
Platform-aware launchers, dependency handling, and CPU/MPS fallbacks for macOS compatibility.
approach: Preserve provenance and deterministic record identity through each ingestion stage.
Retrieve candidates before reranking; investigate entity-alias and language-related failure cases with real inputs.
Make hardware-dependent components optional so the application can run across Windows and Apple Silicon.
projects.result: An integrated client workstream connecting heterogeneous media to structured knowledge, with verified compatibility work on Apple Silicon.
projects.metricNote: The count is from a macOS compatibility validation checkpoint. It does not imply universal retrieval accuracy or MPS acceleration for every component.
projects.growth: This project deepened my experience with provenance, retrieval debugging, and the practical dependency issues involved in cross-platform ML software.
projects.alt: Actual Image-to-KG demo showing a retrieved answer with source-paragraph references and supporting media.

projects.name: Retail Analytics
projects.alt: Actual retail analytics demo showing shopper tracks and colored shelf-zone polygons in an overhead store view.
projects.headline: Connect shopper tracks to the store layout.
projects.summary: Person detection and tracking combined with shelf/zone geometry, trajectory outputs, and segmentation-assisted ROI mapping.
projects.problem: Detections alone do not describe a shopper's movement through a store. Useful analysis requires identities across frames and an association between tracks and the store's spatial layout.
projects.role: I built a retail-video analytics proof of concept, experimented with tracking methods, connected tracks to zones, and developed shelf/rack segmentation and polygon-cleanup logic.
delivered: Detection/tracking overlays and structured trajectory outputs for downstream analysis.
Track-to-zone association using configured shelf and region polygons.
SAM3-assisted shelf/rack segmentation with custom geometry and polygon cleanup for ROI mapping.
approach: Evaluate tracking behavior on retail footage rather than relying only on frame-level detections.
Keep track identity and spatial zone association explicit in the output.
Combine segmentation masks with application-specific geometry to build useful region boundaries.
projects.result: A working multi-video client POC with demonstrable tracking and zone association, plus an automatic ROI-mapping workstream.
projects.metricNote: This is a proof of concept. No store-wide production KPI, identity accuracy, or commercial deployment result is claimed.
projects.growth: The work reinforced the importance of temporal consistency and geometry: model outputs need spatial and application logic before they become useful analytics.

projects.name: Point-cloud Segmentation & Planning
projects.alt: Actual project output: a segmented 3D point cloud with structural obstacles, traversal cells, and colored path-planning markers.
projects.headline: From an unstructured scan to traversable space.
projects.summary: A C++/PCL pipeline separating structural geometry, constructing traversable space, and computing shortest paths with A*.
projects.problem: A raw 3D point cloud needs geometric interpretation before a planner can reason about ground, structural obstacles, and a possible route.
projects.role: I implemented point-cloud segmentation, navigation preprocessing, and A* path planning for a client project.
delivered: Segmented ground, cylindrical pillars, and remaining wall structures.
Traversable-area processing using surface normals, RANSAC, outlier rejection, and octree representation.
A* shortest-path computation with cost-map and path visualizations.
approach: Use geometric structure to distinguish ground and obstacles.
Build the spatial representation before applying graph search.
Visualize segmentation and planning stages so errors can be inspected at their source.
projects.result: A completed point-cloud pipeline with segmented structural layers and a visualized shortest path.
projects.metricNote: The demonstrated result is point-cloud segmentation and planning. It is not a deployed autonomous navigation stack or a depth-camera metrology system.
projects.growth: This project developed my ability to turn geometric data into a representation that a downstream algorithm can use, and to debug the stages visually.

projects.name: Multispectral Calibration & OpenDroneMap
projects.headline: Preserve the measurement, not just the image.
projects.summary: Four-band Parrot Sequoia calibration and C++ integration into an OpenDroneMap workflow with 16-bit orthomosaic output.
projects.problem: Multispectral aerial images need geometric and radiometric correction, while a photogrammetry workflow must preserve their useful measurement information.
projects.role: At the Institute of Space Technology, I built/prototyped calibration steps and integrated C++ code into OpenDroneMap for an HEC-funded unmanned aerial forest-management R&D project.
delivered: Calibration stages for vignetting, dark-current correction, geometric undistortion, and radiometric calibration.
Processing of Green, Red, Red Edge, and NIR imagery from the Parrot Sequoia camera.
An OpenDroneMap workflow extension preserving 16-bit orthomosaic output, alongside Linux build and integration work.
approach: Treat the camera model and radiometric corrections as part of the measurement pipeline.
Prototype corrections and integrate the working stages into the existing C++ photogrammetry workflow.
Preserve pixel depth through output rather than discarding information during conversion.
projects.result: Delivered calibration and photogrammetry integration work during Aug 2019–Jun 2020, including four-band processing and 16-bit orthomosaic capability.
projects.metricNote: The registry also records approximately 12.1 seconds per image for the calibration pipeline. These are historical workflow results, not a benchmark on current hardware.
projects.growth: This was formative work: learning camera models, radiometry, C++, and photogrammetry while solving a real research problem outside my initial comfort zone.
projects.evidenceNote: The public ODM release note corroborates the feature and timeline; it does not establish individual authorship of the entire multispectral feature set.

projects.name: Secure Access
projects.headline: Live camera input. Identity-aware feedback.
projects.summary: A public webcam application connecting face detection, recognition, and tracking to immediate access feedback.
projects.problem: A live-camera application needs to recognize authorized people while keeping video processing and application feedback responsive.
projects.role: I developed and taught the face detection, alignment, recognition, tracking, and access-logic workflow as a public OpenCV project.
delivered: Continuous camera acquisition with face detection and tracking.
Face alignment and embedding/distance-based recognition logic.
Authorized-access decisions and responsive user feedback in an application workflow.
approach: Connect recognition and tracking so the workflow can use identity over time.
Use multiprocessing alongside tracking for continuous frame processing.
Make the complete workflow understandable and reproducible through source code and teaching materials.
projects.result: A completed public application and teaching project demonstrating live-video recognition and interactive CV.
projects.metricNote: This is a public teaching application, not a certified physical access-control product. No security certification or measured latency is claimed.
projects.growth: Building and teaching the application strengthened both my real-time CV integration skills and my ability to explain an engineering workflow clearly.
projects.alt: Actual Secure Access demo frame showing tracked face recognition and authorized-access feedback.
